payload.title: [calls-isolation-1] Call records and events are not app-id scoped — call commands ignore the connection's appId
payload.description:
AUDIT FINDING calls-isolation-1 (medium/isolation, confidence=medium, verify-votes +2/-0)

FILE: apps/server/src/sync/gateway.ts
LINES: 1696-1744

WHAT: Every other write path in the gateway threads #appIdFor(client) into store reads/writes/fan-out for FR-153 app isolation (e.g. append/object/presence at 1390, 1462, 1532). #handleCallCommand builds the CallActor from principal.tenantId/userId/deviceId only (lines 1696-1700) and never passes appId. CallControlPlane then writes all CallRoom/CallInvite/CallParticipant records via this.#store.upsertObject(tenantId, type, id, value) and appendEvent({tenantId,...}) with no appId (call-control-plane.ts 688-721), which lands them in the tenant's default app namespace (store.ts upsertObject tenant form is not app-partitioned). Reads (listInvites/listParticipants/#readRoom) are likewise app-agnostic.

IMPACT: In a multi-app tenant deployment, all calls share one per-tenant namespace regardless of which app the caller is pinned to. A principal authenticated under app A operating on a call created under app B is not isolated at the control-plane store level (membership/state lookups cross app boundaries), and object-delta fan-out of call records does not carry the originating appId, so app-scoped subscribers' visibility of call records is inconsistent with the rest of the system's FR-153 guarantees.

SUGGESTED FIX: Thread appId (#appIdFor(client)) into the CallActor / CallControlPlane and into every store read/write + appendEvent so call records and events are partitioned per app exactly like objects, streams, and presence.
